descriptionHtml:
Approach · TC-23 Dictation Fidelity · S17 Dictation timing: Dictate to 'Listening…' and Stop to text, short and long takes

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U8 Dictation never leaves the physician waiting with nothing: a start or finish that fails is retried and then shown as a clear message, and the AI call time is logged separately from the total. (UAT 3.5)
  • T3 Dictation does not crash the tab. (TFA-94423 AC 8)

Test design technique: Performance (performance) — Measure the time and check it is within the required seconds.

Given Same setup as S01, both contexts

When 10 cycles of H-01 and 3 cycles of the ten-sentence take (the L-03 sentences), timing each step

Then Per cycle: tap-to-ready ms, Stop-to-text ms, browser-side Stop-to-final ms (the AI's own transcription time) and prepareSession durationMs / providerMs (session start) are recorded; the tab stays alive and the microphone is released after each take

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): No UAT target for dictation (Q10): times are data for Daniela. Any step over 30 s is flagged for review (3.5 investigation limit), not failed; a step that ends in neither text nor a message is a Fail of U8. prepareSession times are reported as 'session start' only: live transcription runs browser to OpenAI over WebRTC, so aiCallLog has no AI time that matches Stop-to-text, and …

Where it ran: local aicheck-dictation (dictation AI checks); test method PERF · Performance timing; lane planned in the matrix: AI check (automated)

S17 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/TC-23.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Triage (2026-10-14): 1 row.

Issue type: Test issue · environment local · tickets TFA-94423 ready for qa

Partly judged: the app gets ready within about 0.5–1.4 s, but how long real transcription takes is blocked on the OpenAI key approval.

Evidence: allure-results/9ca241bc…: 22/22 app-side cells pass with the scripted far end (tap→ready 545–1424 ms). Dictate→Listening against OpenAI and Stop→text need the live engine, so they wait on the key.

Duplicate: the same issue as TC-23/S01; read that one (the kept one). This result carries the label "Duplicate", so a filter can leave it out.

Environment: local — main e02167f, local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane aicheck-dictation.

Test method: PERF · Performance timing; secondary: AICHECK · AI output check — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on local; Source: aicheck-dictation.

UAT item: TC-23 Dictation Fidelity · Section: A5 · Cross-Cutting · Scenario: TC-23/S17

Dictation timing: Dictate to 'Listening…' and Stop to text, short and long takes

Tickets: TFA-94423 Implement GPT-live medical mode for active dictation (ready for qa)

New local lane aicheck-dictation: status blocked in aicheck-dictation/results.json → blocked (blocked).

How it is tested (aicheck-dictation/plan.json, automatable: partly): per take: Dictate tap -> mic track enabled, Stop -> text in field, Stop -> last transcription.completed event on the data channel, prepareSession durationMs/providerMs ('session start'); tabAlive and micReleased after each take. Live gives the timings; scripted mode records tap-to-ready (real prepareSession, local far end) and the tabAlive/micReleased checks. — Timings are record-only data (Q10); the Stop-to-text and AI-time numbers need the live engine (gated).

Detail:

22/22 app-side cells pass with the scripted far end. Still open: Dictate→Listening against OpenAI, Stop→text and the AI's own time need the live engine — laneB-preconditions not met: the local OPENAI_API_KEY ends …PUMA and there is no OK on record from Quinn that it is not the key dev uses (her 2026-10-09 notes say it may be), so no audio was sent to OpenAI. Run after that OK: QA_DICT_MODE=live QA_DICTATION_LIVE_OK=PUMA scripts/aicheck-dictation/run.sh. Timings (record-only, scripted far end): tap→ready 545–1424 ms; prepareSession 'session start' [392,300,587,436,312,349] ms. This raw file is from the earlier run, which ran before the review fix and used the real prepareSession: each take minted one OpenAI client secret (client.realtime.clientSecrets.create on api.openai.com) with the local key …PUMA — no audio, but the gated key was used.

Evidence: 2 attached.

Dev run: skipped: local-only — local-only — Lane B (dictation-ai runner, not built): it plays a fixed synthetic voice into the app's own Dictate through a getUserMedia shim (no real microphone or speaker) on a fresh @roundai.test account, spending the local OpenAI key (laneB-preconditions).. This local result replaces that dev entry (the scenario appears once).
